answer: A song that holds real significance for me is a particular folk melody that was often played in my home when I was a child. It is a bhatiali song, a traditional kind of boatman's song from our river region, slow and full of longing. I first heard it as a young boy, and it is deeply tied to memories of my grandparents. My grandfather used to hum it while we sat on the veranda of their village home, watching the boats move slowly along the river in the evening. Whenever I hear it now, it instantly transports me back to those [[carefree]] childhood days. What makes it so important is not the song itself but the powerful [[nostalgia]] it evokes. The gentle melody and heartfelt lyrics have a wonderfully [[soothing]] quality that I find comforting. It is amazing how a single piece of music can carry such emotional weight and instantly bring back a whole era of your life. Honestly, I think this is the true power of music; it becomes intertwined with our memories. My grandfather is in his eighties now, and he still hums it sometimes when we visit, which makes it feel even more precious to me. Listening to it now sometimes brings a tear to my eye, in the best possible way. It is a [[cherished]] reminder of my roots and the people I love, and I hope to pass it on one day, perhaps starting with my little nephew, so that it [[lives on]] in our family.

followUps.q: Do young people in your country still listen to folk music?
followUps.answer: Fewer than before, but it has had a revival recently. Some young bands mix folk songs with modern instruments, which has introduced them to a whole new audience, especially online.

followUps.q: Can you play or sing this song yourself?
followUps.answer: I can sing a few lines, though not very well! I once tried learning it on a harmonium, but I didn't have the patience. Maybe I will try again with proper [[guidance]].

note: Named the genre (bhatiali), added grandfather humming on the village veranda (still alive, in his eighties) and passing it to his nephew; added [[lives on]].
